title: Graceful exit framework for legacy chatstream and client SDKs
creator: Asha Kapoor
summary: Define and execute a multi-phase, low-friction deprecation plan to remove the legacy ChatStream transport and compatibility shim from our hosted API and official client SDKs while minimizing customer disruption. Deliverables: timelines, SDK changes, automated adaptation tooling, telemetry and rollback criteria, comms templates, and acceptance gates.
background_and_rationale: The legacy ChatStream endpoints and compatibility shim were originally introduced to support older clients and streaming transports. Over time they have increased maintenance burden, prevented runtime optimizations (continuous batching, prefix cache reuse), and complicated rollout of advanced fallbacks. This initiative creates a documented, repeatable framework for retiring the old transport and shim, including automated client guidance and server-side compatibility mitigations during the transition.
goals: Provide a clear, customer-friendly migration timeline with milestone dates and opt-out windows
Reduce runtime complexity by removing the compatibility shim and legacy endpoints from hosted and Dedicated control planes
Deliver SDK updates across languages that surface migration warnings and offer automatic adaptation where possible
Instrument telemetry and alerting to detect migration regressions and customer impact within 24h
Publish communication bundles (email, status page, and In-Console banners) and self-service migration docs
out_of_scope: Full protocol translation for third-party proxies (customers with custom gateways must adapt independently)
Major model architecture changes unrelated to the transport removal
timeline_and_phases: Phase 0 (Discovery, Feb 2026): compatibility inventory, top customers list, SDK callsites catalog
Phase 1 (Beta tooling & SDK warnings, Mar 2026): ship opt-in SDK adapters that detect legacy transport and recommend unified endpoints
Phase 2 (Gradual enforcement, Apr 2026): server-side soft-deprecation with increased response warnings and telemetry gating; Console banners enabled
Phase 3 (Hard deprecation window, Jun 2026): disable legacy endpoints on non-dedicated hosted backends with a minimum 30-day notice to remaining customers
Phase 4 (Removal & cleanup, Aug 2026): remove compatibility shim from SDKs and code paths, ship final release notes and cost/latency improvements summary
acceptance_criteria: All official SDKs (JS, Python, Go, Java) include a migration warning in vX.Y and provide optional automatic adapter for common request shapes
Telemetry shows <1% of traffic hitting legacy endpoints after Phase 2 for at least two rolling weeks before moving to Phase 3
At least 95% of identified high-usage customers have either migrated or are on a documented mitigation plan prior to the hard deprecation date
Rollout runbook executed in staging with rollback validated within 30 minutes
Documentation and comms bundle published with step-by-step migration guide and FAQ
rollout_checklist: Confirm ENG tickets for runtime removal tasks are tracked and estimated
Ship SDK beta with opt-in adapter and warning message
Enable Console banner and status page timeline
Notify top 50 customers via CSMs and include migration support offer
Run canary in dedicated region and validate telemetry coverage
Finalize fallback policies and automatic model variant routing if compatibility mismatch occurs
telemetry_and_monitoring: Alert: legacy_transport_request_rate > 5% of baseline for 6 hours
Dashboard panels: migration progress by customer cohort, error spike detection, latency delta pre/post removal
Weekly migration health digest for PM/Eng/CSM teams
communication_plan: T-minus 60d: In-Console banner + status page announcement with API timeline
T-minus 30d: Direct emails to owners and CSM outreach to customers with non-zero legacy traffic
T-minus 14d: Required SDK upgrade notice in changelogs and migration how-to
Post-removal: publish a post-mortem with latency/cost benefits and lessons learned
safety_and_fallback_policies: Soft-deprecation responses include structured hint in response payload pointing to migration doc
Server-side fallback to an older but compatible model variant for customers with unaddressed requests (limited to 5% traffic) during Phase 2
Automatic re-enablement plan if critical downstream failures observed (requires cross-team approval)
testing_and_validation: Unit and integration tests for SDK adapters and warning paths
Load tests that show continuous-batching and KV-cache improvements after shim removal
Customer-facing staging environment with opt-in migration testing for top 20 customers
Chaos test: simulate degraded adapter and validate rollback runbook
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large customers with custom proxies will be unable to upgrade quickly — Mitigation: offer dedicated migration engineering time and on-prem compatibility bridge
Risk: Unexpected client breakage causing higher error rates — Mitigation: phased traffic gating and immediate rollback window, mobile SDK snapshot back-compat builds
Risk: Insufficient telemetry coverage — Mitigation: instrument additional hooks and default sampling for legacy transport events
